title: Create a wiretap error for malformed records within a file
description:
Add a case where the file is (mostly) good, but a record is found to be malformed, so skip to the next one.

Fixes #20511

notes.body: mentioned in issue #20511
Unsure if the "size check" should be a layer higher?  Do we want to keep a custom block with a Private Enterprise Number of zero size?

I think Jim's capture file in #20511 is a bit contrived as it looks like it contains assorted PENs with no data.    Previous Netflix code _required_ 4 bytes after the PEN, but using the sample capture I was able to allow a custom block with nothing after the PEN.  Unfortunately the original "documentation" linked to is either gone or not accessible to me, but still has the question, if the vendor _requires_ bytes after the PEN, is the previous behavior "better" and we need to focus on just ignoring the "bad" custom block and continue to read the capture.

> I think Jim's capture file in #20511 is a bit contrived as it looks like it contains assorted PENs with no data.

If you mean the capture file in https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/issues/20511#note_2497025668, that is most definitely a rather contrived capture file - and a pretty impressive contrivance.

Try giving it a name that ends with ".pdf" and open it. (Yes, it works, and shows you a document.)

Then try giving it a name that ends with ".pcapng" and open it. (Yes, it works, and shows you a capture that, I suspect, is an example of one of the topics described in the document.)

If you open it in Fileshark mode (i.e., view it as a capture file), you'll notice that the first custom block contains...

...a header for a PDF file.

My hat's off to its creators.

> if the vendor _requires_ bytes after the PEN, is the previous behavior "better" and we need to focus on just ignoring the "bad" custom block and continue to read the capture.

It's up to the code for that particular organization's custom blocks to handle an incorrectly-formed custom block; it's not up to Wireshark's generic custom-block handling code to decide, based on zero information about the requirements of that organization, what blocks are OK and what blocks aren't.

And having a way for wiretap code to mark a record as being malformed, with an error message indicating the particular malformation, rather than stopping the read, so that Wireshark/TShark/sharkd/whatever can show it as being malformed, but show all the subsequent packets, seems to be what the submitter of #20511 wanted - @jim.young?

The captures I attached in #20511 were indeed contrived simply for testing purposes.

Wireshark handles pcapng Custom Blocks (CB) with arbitrary (but unknown by Wireshark) PEN values without issue. But certain CBs having the Netflix PEN would halt Wireshark from processing any further blocks.  From a naive pcapng reader's point-of-view (one that knows nothing about what is or is what is not a valid Netflix CB) the basic pcapng block structure is fine, and the Netflix PEN CBs in the contrived captures can be easily skipped. I felt that Wireshark could be improved to be more helpful when presented with a pcapng CB with a known PEN but having a non-conforming payload.

> I felt that Wireshark could be improved to be more helpful when presented with a pcapng CB with a known PEN but having a non-conforming payload.

E.g., if a block (not necessarily a CB!) is non-conforming in a way that doesn't prevent reading subsequent blocks (e.g., if the block header and trailer are OK, but the block content is non-conforming), instead of returning an error from libwiretap, return success, but with some field in the`wtap_rec` structure indicating a read error and with a pointer to a string giving the read error details.  Wireshark and TShark could put that information in the Frame section, and not bother doing any further dissection.  They might *also* not write out that record in a Save or Export, might not allow adding comments to it, etc.

It gets more complicated for records that *don't* show up in the packet list, and that might affect the handling of othe records, such as IDBs (you need to handle them to the extent of not changing the IDB ordinal numbers of later IDBs, and you might not even be able to dissect packets for that interface if the problem is that there's no block data and thus no LINKTYPE_ value for the interface) or NRBs (although that's just "we have to fall back on other mechanisms to resolve names and addresses") or DSBs (although that's just "sorry, we can't decrypt this").

But we could start with just doing this for CBs and  leave this issue open for work on other block types.

Would a solution to this problem (#20511) be backported?  At this point, I don't think the current patch is the "right" solution, but it's closer to a bugfix than the enhancement of adding to the wtap_rec structure (the "right" fix).

Because this has all be good discussion, but I think it's leading to this MR being rejected (closed).

With the updated approach, I think this is okay to add to master, but wouldn't backport.  The capture in question was "contrived", but has allowed for a better architecture to handle "poorly formatted" files
